text:
alex: Quick help — deploying vectorizer to payments namespace. IRSA role created via Terraform, service account annotated by helm chart, but pod fails with KMS decrypt AccessDenied. Role ARN in annotation matches, role shows up in IAM. Any ideas?

maria: Did you create a kms_grant for the role? KMS key policy must allow the grantee to use the key

alex: I thought the grant would be created by TF: here's snippet
```
resource "aws_iam_role" "vectorizer_irsa" {
  name = "payments-vectorizer-irsa"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_trust.json
}
resource "aws_kms_grant" "vectorizer_grant" {
  name = "vectorizer-grant"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.payments.id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vectorizer_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```
and helm creates the serviceaccount with annotation: `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: <role arn>`

jon: The common race is helm creates SA and annotates first, then TF creates role and grant later. IRSA works if the role exists by the time of pod start because STS needs to assume it. Does your pod restart after terraform apply?

alex: I redeployed workloads after apply — still AccessDenied. k8s logs show: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/payments-vectorizer-irsa/i-xxxxxxxx is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource` — note assumed-role principal is the node instance role, not the IRSA role

maria: That usually means the token projected from the SA didn't map to the role because the oidc provider trust or annotation didn't match. Check the assume_role_policy for `StringEquals: {"oidc.eks.amazonaws.com:sub": "system:serviceaccount:payments:vectorizer"}` — if you used wildcard or wrong namespace it'll fail.

alex: my assume doc uses `data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_trust` generated like
```
statement {
  effect = "Allow"
  principals { type = "Federated"; identifiers = [aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.oidc.arn] }
  actions = ["sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"]
  condition { test = "StringEquals"; variable = "oidc.eks.amazonaws.com:sub"; values = ["system:serviceaccount:payments:vectorizer"] }
}
```

jon: Also check the EKS oidc provider audience — sometimes we use a different provider resource for staging vs prod. Another gotcha: if you created a KMS key policy that only allows principals from payments account, you still need to either add the role ARN to the key policy principals or use the grant (which you did). Make sure the grant creation actually succeeded and is present in the key's grants.

maria: For TF ordering: add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role.vectorizer_irsa]` to aws_kms_grant so the role is present before the grant is created. Grants created against non-existent ARNs can behave oddly. Also confirm the grant isn't being overwritten by a later key rotation or schedule.

alex: adding depends_on fixed the grant apply timing but the pod still used node role. Turns out helm created SA with annotation `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` set, but our cluster admission webhook rewrites annotations unless the SA is created with the annotation in the initial manifest. The fix: create the k8s serviceaccount with Terraform `kubernetes_service_account` and set annotation there, then set the chart value `createServiceAccount=false` so helm doesn't touch it. After switching to TF-managed SA, pod immediately assumed the right role and KMS decrypt succeeded. :tada:

jon: Nice. For future, you can also create a small rolling restart job or use a post-apply `kubectl rollout restart` hook to ensure pods pick up new SA annotations after infra changes.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: saw 1 rolling restart for payments/vectorizer after SA recreation — passed health checks

alex: thanks all, leaving notes in the infra runbook about depends_on and TF-managed SA for IRSA+KMS use-cases.
